props.title: A DJ for hire in Denver for weddings and corporate parties.
props.lede: The band has played its last song, and nobody’s ready to go home. That’s when you want a great DJ. You can book one on their own, or have one take over after the band.

headingText.html: A DJ is an excellent choice for an office holiday party, a company launch, a milestone birthday or a wedding reception.

props.headingNote: Tell us what you have in mind, from the music to what the DJ wears, and we’ll plan it with you. Here’s how booking through Signet works.

props.title: Adding a DJ after the live band
props.lede: Already booking a band? It’s easy to add a DJ to keep the dancing going after the band finishes. When the band’s last set ends, the DJ can pick up through the same sound system, so the music doesn’t stop.

props.html: For a Denver holiday party, many hosts book a duo for cocktails and dinner and a DJ for the rest of the event, and we’ll plan the handoff with you when we go over the flow of the evening. Hiring a DJ on their own, with production lighting, can run $2,500 to $6,000 in the Denver, Colorado market.
That range comes from published 2026 market guides. We quote each date one-by-one.

props.title: Add a live bass or saxophone player
props.lede: A musician on bass or saxophone can play along with the DJ, so your guests get a live performance to watch, too. It’s a great way to keep people dancing late at a wedding or a company party, so just let us know if you’d like it.

props.html: Want live music earlier on? Tejas Singh can start as a duo, grow to a quartet and hand off to the DJ, and you’ll find more great acts on our roster.

rows.text: A DJ is one of the most popular choices for an office holiday party, from a downtown Denver hotel ballroom to your own office.
Book a DJ for a launch, a closing dinner that turns into a party or a member event that runs late.
A DJ is a great way to get everybody dancing at a milestone birthday, an anniversary or a Halloween party.
Many couples book live musicians for the ceremony and the cocktail hour, then a DJ from the first dance to the last song.

props.html: Wondering what it all costs? Take a look at the cost guide. Still deciding? Here’s our take on band or DJ for a Denver wedding or company party.

props.title: Can I choose what the DJ plays?
props.lede: Yes, as much as you’d like. You can build the list yourself, give us a do-not-play list and leave the rest to the DJ, or just tell us about your crowd and let the DJ take it from there.

props.html: Open format means the DJ plays all kinds of music, so you can mix as many styles as you’d like.

props.title: Venues
props.lede: We’d pick {name} for live music at these venues.

props.html: Have a question about curfews or volume limits? You can find more answers on our full question list.

items.a: It can be as loud as you want, up to what your venue allows. During dinner or a toast, the DJ can keep it low enough for easy talking, and then turn it up once people are dancing. If your venue has a sound limit, let us know and the DJ will work within it.

items.q: How late can the DJ play?
items.a: As late as the venue allows. If you think your party might run long, just let us know when you book.

Yes. The DJ will play your requests, and guests’ requests when they fit. We’d suggest spending a little time on your do-not-play list, and if a guest asks for something that might clear the dance floor, the DJ can suggest something else.

props.title: Looking for a DJ in Denver? Send us the date and the venue, and tell us if you’ve got a band, too.
props.lede: We can bring a DJ on their own or plan live music around them, and we’ll reply with availability and costs.
